title: Managed Backup: returned remittance principal
content:
For Managed Backup, the returned remittance principal basis governs bank return recording.

## Policy clauses

The completed bank return notice refers to the exact original posted payment.

The bank return must identify the exact posted payment.

Restore the returned principal as a positive amount, up to the original payment amount not already returned.

Copy its method, customer, billing entity and currency.

A partial return uses the distinct bank notice external source reference.

A duplicate bank notice produces no new write.

Any returned payment fee is a separately identifiable return-fee charge under lifecycle and bank-return fee rules, never hidden in returned principal; a waived fee produces no fee posting.

## Authoritative evidence

Before bank return recording, system records must establish this condition for the proposed action: The completed bank return notice refers to the exact original posted payment.

The evidence identifies Event reference, Original source reference, Status, External source reference. Match the action to that evidence by Event reference, Original source reference; these references identify the same proposed business objects.

Returned principal is the absolute magnitude of the returned payment amount, subject to the unreversed original-payment cap.

## Basis Q&A

**What is the stated entry basis?** The completed bank return notice refers to the exact original posted payment.

## Hypothetical case

A hypothetical original payment principal is USD 90 and prior returns total USD 25. The remaining principal available for return is USD 65. A distinct completed bank notice may identify a partial return within that remainder; a duplicated bank notice creates no additional return.
